Hi Sasha — thanks for the context. Attached is a compact questionnaire + a sample CSV layout for token histograms. Below is the exact set of fields that gives us a tight first-pass GPU footprint and SLO/pricing sensitivity: please ask Diego to populate as many as possible.

QUESTIONNAIRE (short form) — please provide numbers where possible:
1) Workload(s) overview
   - Name the workload (chat | batch-summary).
2) Expected peak sustained RPS/window (per workload)
   - e.g., chat: 120 RPS sustained during 09:00-11:00 PT peak; batch: single daily job with 1800 concurrency for 30m.
3) Peak instantaneous burst (RPS) and duration
4) Average prompt length (tokens) and 95th percentile prompt length
5) Average response length (tokens) and 95th percentile response length
6) Prompt/response token histogram (CSV): columns = session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, timestamp, session_duration_seconds
7) Session stickiness / session affinity
   - % of requests that reuse KV cache across calls (e.g., friend_session flows where we send additional user turns)
8) Average and P95 end-to-end latency target (ms) for interactive chat
9) Streaming usage fraction (what % of responses are streamed vs complete-at-once)
10) Typical model variants to serve (name + quantization level)
11) Batch job concurrency and acceptable wall-clock window for completion
12) Availability / SLA requirements (SLOs, maintenance windows tolerated)
13) Data residency / encryption / KMS requirements (if any)
14) Any special request routing or fallback policy (multi-model fallback, region failover)
Optional but helpful:
- Token mix by prompt type (short commands vs long context)
- Typical KV cache size per session (KB)
- Peak concurrent sessions (distinct session IDs)

We'll use this to compute: estimated GPUs, recommended GPU SKUs (v2/v3 family), expected occupancy and oversubscription guardrails, and a candidate pricing cadence (reserved commit + burst).

Attachments: redwood_preflight_checklist.pdf (short checklist), sample CSV (lumina_token_profile_sample.csv).

If Diego can return the CSV by EOD tomorrow we can run a preliminary footprint and share a slide with estimated fleet and a recommended commit range.

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
